MEDICINE 1.0
Conventional
  • Measures in the office, labels a category, adds a pill, adds another
  • Strong outcome data for lowering the number
  • Rarely asks about salt type, standing response, sleep apnea, insulin or minerals
ASSUMPTION WORTH QUESTIONING
"A normal reading means a healthy system."
MEDICINE 2.0
Standard Functional
  • Adds diet, magnesium, CoQ10, stress work
  • Looks for root causes
  • Often a long supplement list without ranking, and "low salt for everyone"
ASSUMPTION WORTH QUESTIONING
"Natural is enough, and more supplements are better."
MEDICINE 3.0
RoVive Method
  • Reads the message: home numbers, standing test, pulse pressure, salt type
  • Finds your lever (pump, pipes, fluid, conductor) and ranks the moves by evidence tier
  • Uses medication smartly: 2 low doses, replace what drains, step down when safe
  • Includes the inner life and the energetic layer, labeled honestly
RoVive 3.0 doesn't stop at integrative medicine. It goes all the way: homeopathy, frequency medicine, somatic healing, metaphysics, and the inner life, because the body, mind, and spirit are inseparable. It always questions, always pushes the boundaries while simplifying, going within, and drawing on common sense and ancient wisdom. Finding balance in our modern world is the journey worth taking. And no protocol is complete without asking why.
◆ The RoVive Clinical Framework
These four stages (Roots, Reveal, Refine, Rise) are the RoVive diagnostic and therapeutic sequence applied to this protocol.
R
ROOTS
The foundational inputs your pressure depends on
›
  • Sodium-to-potassium balance, magnesium, and water
  • Sleep and breathing at night (sleep apnea)
  • Movement: all 4 pumps used daily
  • Blood sugar and insulin steadiness
  • Nervous system load: caffeine, alcohol, stress, screens, loneliness
  • Medications and substances that raise pressure (NSAIDs, decongestants, licorice)
R
REVEAL
Read the message: home tests, then labs in 3 layers
›

Home first: 7-day home average, standing test, pulse pressure, 12-day salt test, and the 10-minute stand test if your pulse jumps.

  1. Standard (Quest via Rupa) ✓ RWC Lab Store: CMP, magnesium, HbA1c, fasting insulin, uric acid, lipids and ApoB, TSH, hs-CRP, urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio, aldosterone-to-renin ratio when indicated.
  2. Functional ✓ RWC Lab Store: RBC magnesium, Omega-3 Index, homocysteine and B12, ferritin, 24-hour urine sodium and potassium, DUTCH Plus for the conductor.
  3. Advanced ✓ RWC Lab Store: MTHFR and broader genetics (3X4), plus a sleep study, 24-hour monitor, pulse wave velocity and calcium score through your clinician.

Sequencing rule: foundational first, act for 8 to 12 weeks, escalate only where a real question remains.

R
REFINE
Pull your lever, in order of leverage
›
  1. Treat sleep apnea if present.
  2. Isometrics 3 days a week plus Zone 2 most days.
  3. Salt by your salt type; a potassium-rich plate; a 25% potassium salt if safe for you.
  4. Steady blood sugar; alcohol and caffeine audit; remove pressure-raising substances.
  5. Breath: slow breathing daily; resisted breathing if you want a bigger effect.
  6. Targeted supplements to fill gaps (magnesium, omega-3, cocoa flavanols, hibiscus, aged garlic).
  7. Medication, when needed, used smartly: 2 low doses, replace what it drains.

The best medicine is the one you actually believe will work. Different people respond to different modalities, not because of placebo, but because belief, expectation, and neurological state are themselves physiological inputs. Choose what resonates.

R
RISE
What success looks like
›
  • Numbers: home average under 120/80 (around 115/75 if you feel well), pulse pressure under 50 and not widening, standing within 10, a 10% to 20% night dip.
  • Felt experience: steady energy, no dizziness on standing, warm hands and feet, deep sleep, a calm baseline.
  • Life capacity: walking hills, lifting grandchildren, training without fear, on the fewest pills that keep you safe.
  • Recheck: seated, standing and your gap every 4 weeks while you change things, then every 3 months.
◆ THE EMOTIONAL ROOT
Physical symptoms are real. And they often have an emotional architecture beneath them, not as weakness, but as the body's intelligence. Unresolved emotional patterns, stored stress, and unconscious adaptations can maintain the very physiology we're trying to change. This isn't about blame. It's about completeness.

The emotional pattern in blood pressure

We even speak of it in pressure words: "under pressure," "about to blow," "keeping a lid on it." Chronic vigilance keeps the sympathetic conductor switched on: adrenaline narrows vessels, the kidneys hold salt, and the heart pushes harder. Suppressed anger and unexpressed grief are not abstractions here; they are a sustained physiological state. And the reverse is just as real: the person who never raises their voice can carry the highest readings.

The sentence: high pressure is often the body holding what the person will not let out.

The best approach is the one you believe will work and will actually do. Different people respond to entirely different modalities; that's not noise, it's biology.

Breath and the vagus

Slow breathing at about 6 a minute, with a long exhale, twice a day. The fastest way to tell the conductor it is safe. Tier 2

Meditation and prayer

Transcendental Meditation has the most pressure data (about 4 points); prayer, contemplative practice and coherence breathing share the same direction. Tier 2

Expressing what is held

Journaling, therapy, somatic work, or saying the hard thing to the right person. Unexpressed grief is a pressure in its own right. Tier 3

Connection

Loneliness predicted pressure climbing faster each year. A walking partner works 2 levers at once. Tier 3

◆ Circle only · Is your heart really a pump? The Cowan question

Love him or hate him, Dr. Thomas Cowan made a lot of people ask this question. His book Human Heart, Cosmic Heart argues the heart is more of a regulator than a pump, building on Rudolf Steiner and on Branko Furst's physiology.

Where Dr. Yoshi thinks he's right: the heart is more than a squeeze, flow has a life of its own at the small scale, and the vessel wall is active. That's why "flow is alive."

Where he parts ways: the evidence that the heart is a real pump is overwhelming, and coronary artery disease is real. Take the curiosity, keep the cardiologist.

◆ There is music in your minerals: the physics, then the poetry

The physics Tier 1: the sodium-potassium pump moves 3 sodium out and 2 potassium in for each ATP it uses (a 3:2 ratio, like a perfect fifth), and it binds ATP as magnesium-ATP: magnesium turns the key. Sodium is about 140 outside your cells; potassium is about 140 inside them, a mirror. Sodium (11) and potassium (19) sit 8 elements apart in the same family, like the same note an octave higher, the pattern that seeded the periodic table. And magnesium sits at the center of every chlorophyll molecule: magnesium is how light becomes life.

The poetry (Circle only) Tier 3: each element gives off its own color of light. Sodium glows yellow-orange, magnesium shows green, potassium a deep red with a touch of violet. Map those onto the chakras: sodium, the solar plexus (fire and outward action); magnesium, the heart (rhythm and relaxation); potassium, root and crown at once (the inside, the stillness). Drop magnesium's green light about 40 octaves into sound and it lands near 526 to 528 hertz, the frequency many call the love frequency. Thinkers like Robert Edward Grant would see the Hermetic principles here: polarity, rhythm, correspondence.

The honest part: turning light into sound is a beautiful game with numbers, not a mechanism. Pick a different line of light and the note shifts. Shared because it inspires, not because it is proven. Take what resonates.

◆ WHERE TO START
NEW TO THIS PROTOCOL
Take 7 days of home readings the right way, plus the standing test. Enter them in the calculator (Labs & Targets). Then, if your home average is under 160/100 and none of the cautions in the Movement pillar apply, start 4 wall-squat holds of 2 minutes, 3 days a week.
ALREADY DOING THE BASICS
Run the 12-day salt test, get a sleep study if you snore or your mornings run high, and check RBC magnesium, fasting insulin, urine albumin and (if resistant or low potassium) the aldosterone-to-renin ratio.

Your targets on one screen

MarkerRoVive target
Home averageUnder 120/80; around 115/75 if you feel well and stand without symptoms
Pulse pressureUnder 50 and not widening (60+ wide, 50 to 59 watch, under 25% of the top number narrow)
Standing at 1 and 3 minutesWithin 10 points; pulse up 10 to 20
Night dip10% to 20%
Salt test, phase 2 vs 1Up 5+ salt-sensitive; down 5+ possibly inverse; in between resistant
Potassium / magnesiumSerum potassium 4.0 to 5.0; serum magnesium 2.0+, RBC upper half
Fasting insulin / HbA1cUnder 7 (ideally 3 to 5) / under 5.4%
Urine albumin-to-creatinineUnder 10 mg/g

The core moves

EDUCATIONAL ONLY · NOT MEDICAL ADVICE · NOT A PRESCRIPTION · REVIEW ANY CHANGE WITH YOUR OWN CLINICIAN, ESPECIALLY IF YOU TAKE BLOOD PRESSURE MEDICATION

Every lever
  • Isometrics: 4 x 2-minute wall squats or handgrip, 3 days a week Tier 1
  • Zone 2 about 150 minutes a week Tier 1
  • Sleep apnea checked and treated Tier 1
  • Slow breathing 5 to 15 minutes daily Tier 2
Fluid lever
  • Salt by your salt type Tier 1
  • 25% potassium salt, if kidneys and medications allow Tier 1
  • Potassium-rich plate; hydrate Tier 1
  • Low on standing: water bolus, salt, compression Tier 2
Pipes lever
  • Steady blood sugar; walk after meals Tier 2
  • Magnesium 300 to 400 mg Tier 1; K2 MK-7 180 mcg Tier 2
  • Cocoa flavanols Tier 2, omega-3 Tier 1; nitrate greens, no antiseptic mouthwash Tier 2
  • Leg swelling: diosmin and hesperidin, horse chestnut Tier 2
Conductor
  • Caffeine and alcohol audit Tier 1
  • Meditation or prayer, connection Tier 2
  • Resisted breathing (IMST) Tier 2
  • Medications: 2 low doses beat 1 high dose; never stop suddenly Tier 1

The sentences

  • Your blood pressure is a message, not a number.
  • Every reading is set by 3 levers, and the conductor works all 3.
  • Don't guess. Test: your salt type, your standing response, your gap.
  • Lower is usually better, if you tolerate it. Protect the bottom number, and listen to how you feel when you stand.
  • High pressure is often the body holding what the person will not let out.

Top 3 failure points

1. Judging by one office number. White-coat and masked patterns mislead in both directions. A week of home readings, measured the right way, is the real picture.
2. "Low salt for everyone." Salt-sensitive people need it; inverse responders can be harmed by it; low-pressure and POTS patterns need more. Test first.
3. Stacking supplements instead of pulling levers. A wall squat, a sleep study and a potassium salt outperform a shelf of capsules.
